summary.intent: Complete the v1.1 hardening block (phases 51–55) by discussing all 5 phases in parallel, planning them concurrently in isolated git worktrees, executing Phase 51, and running its full ship loop (verify → secure → validate → simplify → CodeRabbit review).
summary.outcome: All 5 hardening phases discussed and planned (21 total plans); Phase 51 fully executed and ship-loop validated — a real cross-crate build break was caught and fixed, security audit returned 15/15 CLOSED, Nyquist validation confirmed 0 gaps, and 5 CodeRabbit zeroization findings were applied. Phases 52–55 are planned and ready to execute.

workflow: Create per-phase git worktrees manually (not via Agent isolation: worktree) for persistent background planning/execution — gives each phase its own git index, preventing lock collisions across concurrent agents
Worktree setup sequence: checkout main in main tree → git worktree add on the phase branch → pnpm i in the worktree (hooks require node_modules via absolute hooksPath)
Stop any running background agent before creating worktrees to avoid index.lock contention on the branch being checked out
Run CodeRabbit CLI review BEFORE opening the PR so the PR opens already-clean — avoids a separate fixup PR cycle
git verify-commit allowedSignersFile warning is a local trust-config gap, not a missing signature — the commit carries a valid SSH signature block and verifies on GitHub
cargo fmt reformatting of out-of-scope files during execution must be immediately reverted with git checkout -- on those files before the next commit, not left as unrelated churn in the plan commit
execute-phase's cargo test -p <crate> gate is insufficient for phases that change public return types — add cargo check --workspace after execution to catch cross-crate consumers
Discussing all phases first before planning any gives better scope alignment (e.g., dropping #15 from Phase 51 before the planner ran) — avoids planning work that needs to be replanned
